methods.notes: The integration discovers the meter by advertised local name alone (prefix "Keto-Mojo", connectable advertisements); it does not match on a service UUID, and whether the meter advertises 0003cdd0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b0131 is not shown. The name may carry trailing NUL bytes, which the integration strips before display. The meter advertises while it is switched on (the integration syncs whenever it sees an advertisement); the manual gives automatic shut-off two minutes after the last action.

device.name: Keto-Mojo GK+ Blood Glucose and Ketone Meter
device.notes:
A handheld fingerstick meter that reads blood glucose and blood beta-ketone from two kinds of test strip, keeps up to 1000 results in memory, and syncs them to the vendor phone app over BLE. Over BLE it is a read-only data logger: a client asks for the glucose unit, the serial number and the whole stored history, and the meter answers on a notification characteristic. Nothing here starts a test or changes a setting.
The service is the vendor's (VivaChek's), not the Bluetooth SIG Glucose Profile (0x1808). Frames are bracketed by 7b ... 7d and close with a CRC-16 whose two bytes are each split into two nibble bytes, so the check can never contain a 7b or 7d. Each stored result is a 9-byte record: date and time to the minute, a value encoded as two base-100 digits, a meal-marker byte and a type byte that separates glucose, ketone, GKI-mode pairs and control-solution tests.
The meter accepts one BLE connection at a time, so the vendor app must be closed while another client syncs. Readings are a personal log, not a basis for treatment — see safety_advisory.

openness.notes: No vendor publication. One open-source client, whose README says the protocol was worked out independently for interoperability and contains no vendor code. A single source: nothing here has a second, independent confirmation yet.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The integration connects, subscribes and writes with no pairing or bonding step and no application-layer login. The vendor app's "pairing" flow (manual, link to the vendor's Bluetooth connection page) is an app-side association that also sets the clock; whether it creates an OS-level bond is not established.

exclusivity.recovery: Close (force-stop) the Keto-Mojo app on every phone that has synced the meter, then connect.

pairing.notes: From the integration's code and README: no pair call, no secret, one connection at a time. Not replayed by this project.

safety_advisory.detail: A third-party client reads the meter's stored history after the fact; it does not take a measurement and adds no accuracy of its own. Display the value, unit and timestamp exactly as the record carries them, and never show a control-solution result (type bytes 0x22 and 0x66) as a reading: those are quality-control tests of strips and solution, not blood. Glucose and ketone are different quantities in different units — do not mix them on one axis. Timestamps are the meter's own local clock with no time zone, and a meter whose clock was never set (or was reset by a battery change) stamps results with the wrong date. The vendor's own manual says app data is not for medical care reference; the same applies with more force to a client built from this spec, which is experimental and unaffiliated with Keto-Mojo or VivaChek. The manufacturer's instructions for use and a healthcare professional govern any treatment decision.
safety_advisory.summary: Readings synced from the meter are for information only and must never be used to decide an insulin or other medication dose.

credentials.notes: No PIN, key or account token is used by the open client.
stored_on_device: Up to 1000 stored results with date and time
Glucose unit, clock, alarms, meal-marker and ketone-warning settings

factory_reset.description: The GK+ manual covers set-up mode, alarms, markers and battery replacement, and says results survive a battery change; it describes no reset and no memory clear. Memory is a ring of 1000 results, the oldest overwritten first. No BLE command to clear memory is known.
factory_reset.effect: Unknown. The manual documents no factory reset and no way to clear the stored results.

methods.description: The sync as the Home Assistant integration runs it: connect, enable notifications on 0003cdd1, then write three fixed frames to 0003cdd2 one after another, each time waiting for its answer before the next.
methods.name: Connect, subscribe, read history

steps.action: Close the Keto-Mojo app on every phone that has synced this meter — the meter accepts one BLE connection at a time.
Switch the meter on (press the main button, or insert a strip) so it advertises.
steps.expect: An advertisement whose local name begins Keto-Mojo.

steps.action: Connect and enable notifications on 0003cdd1-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b0131; wait about 0.5 s.

steps.expect: A unit reply frame beginning 7b 01 20 01 10 aa aa 00 01.
A serial reply frame beginning 7b 01 20 01 10 77 aa 00 10.

steps.action: Write fetch_all_records and collect notifications until the end-of-records frame.
steps.expect: One record frame per stored result, then 7b 01 20 01 10 d1 66 00 00 0b 09 03 04 7d.

steps.action: Disconnect, so the vendor app can connect again.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision for reading: no account, network or bond. The vendor app's sync also sets the meter's clock from the phone (manual, "Synching Your Meter with the Smartphone"), but the command that does so is not known; without the app the clock is set on the meter itself in its set-up mode (hold the main button for 3 seconds with the meter off).

rejoin.notes: BLE-only and unbonded as far as is known: any central can read the meter once the current one disconnects.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The three request frames and the end-of-records frame are copied byte for byte from an open-source integration that its author runs against a GK+ (firmware SW2071323011A001, meter set to mg/dL). The record, unit and serial worked examples in payload_formats are constructed here from the integration's decoder, with an invented serial and a frame check computed by the derived CRC rule; no raw notification has been published.

Source of the two characteristic UUIDs, the three request frames, the end-of-records frame, the unit and serial reply headers and codes, the 9-byte record layout with its base-100 value, the type-byte and meal-nibble enums, the unit scaling, the write-without-response and notify flow with its timeouts, and the "Keto-Mojo" name matcher. README supplies the service UUID, the VivaChek attribution and the one-connection limit. Facts only; no code transcribed.

artifacts.description: Memory of 1000 dated results (oldest overwritten), pre/post-meal and control-result markers, control results excluded from averages, measurement ranges, two AAA cells, two-minute auto-off, set-up mode entry, and that app sync sets the meter clock. This edition is mmol/L-only; US meters show mg/dL.

evidence.documentation_review: One open-source client and the vendor manual, read 2026-10-25. The client's README says it was developed independently with no vendor code. The frame layout beyond what the client checks (address, status and length bytes) is inferred from the four literal frames and the two reply headers, and the check algorithm was derived from those frames.
evidence.open_questions: The header bytes and length of a record frame (unchecked by the client); the BLE dump order; the low nibble of the meal byte; any further type codes; the clock-set command the vendor app uses; whether the meter advertises its service UUID; whether the characteristics accept write with response; and whether an mmol/L meter's glucose really uses tenths (the client's author tested only mg/dL).

EndOfRecords.description: Sent after the last RecordFrame; a client stops collecting when it sees it. A literal frame from the integration.
parse_rules: Match the whole frame 7b 01 20 01 10 d1 66 00 00 0b 09 03 04 7d (cmd 0xd1, status 0x66, len 0).
Whether the meter sends it for an empty memory, and whether it is the last notification before the meter goes quiet, is not shown.

RecordFrame.description: One stored result, notified on 0003cdd1 after fetch_all_records. 23 bytes: a 9-byte header, the 9-byte record at bytes 9-17, the 4-byte check and 7d. The integration reads only bytes 9-17; header bytes 5-6 of a record frame (shown here as dd aa, by analogy with the unit and serial replies) and the length (shown as 00 09) are not checked by it and are unconfirmed.

fields.description: Byte 9, uint8 binary (not BCD): years since 2000.
fields.name: year

fields.description: Byte 12, uint8, 0-23 (24-hour, whatever the display setting).
fields.name: hour

fields.description: Byte 13, uint8, 0-59. No seconds are stored.
fields.name: minute

fields.description: Byte 14, uint8: the value's hundreds (base-100 high digit). raw = byte14 x 100 + byte15 — NOT a 16-bit integer.
fields.name: value_hundreds

fields.description: Byte 15, uint8, 0-99: the value's base-100 low digit.
fields.name: value_units

fields.description: Byte 16, high nibble. Low nibble not decoded by any client.
fields.name: meal_marker

fields.description: Value of a glucose or glucose-control record when the meter unit is mg/dL: raw as-is.
fields.name: glucose_mg_dl

fields.description: Value of a glucose or glucose-control record when the meter unit is mmol/L: raw / 10.
fields.name: glucose_mmol_l

fields.description: Value of a ketone or ketone-control record, always: raw / 100.
fields.name: ketone_mmol_l

parse_rules: Concatenate notifications in arrival order and cut frames at 7b ... 7d. A frame whose length byte pair (7-8) is 00 09 and whose bytes 1-17 pass the check is a record; the end-of-records frame (cmd 0xd1, status 0x66, len 0) ends the dump.
Timestamp = (2000 + byte9)-byte10-byte11 byte12:byte13, a naive local time on the meter's clock. Skip a record whose date or time is invalid.

raw = byte14 x 100 + byte15. Scale by record_type and the unit from get_unit: ketone types (0x55, 0x56, 0x66) raw / 100 mmol/L; glucose types (0x11, 0x12, 0x22) raw mg/dL, or raw / 10 mmol/L on a meter set to mmol/L.
Meal marker = high nibble of byte 16: 1 pre-meal, 2 post-meal, anything else general.
Types 0x22 and 0x66 are control-solution tests: never present them as readings, and leave them out of averages, as the meter itself does.
Ignore a record whose type byte is not one of the six listed: the integration drops them, and their meaning is unknown.
GKI-mode pairs (0x12 with 0x56) sit next to each other in the dump. GKI = glucose in mmol/L (mg/dL / 18) divided by ketone in mmol/L, floored to one decimal.
Worked (glucose, pre-meal): 7b 01 20 01 10 dd aa 00 09 1a 0a 11 07 1e 00 5f 10 11 0e 09 0b 07 7d = 2026-10-17 07:30, raw 0 x 100 + 95 = 95 mg/dL (mg/dL meter), pre-meal, glucose.
Worked (glucose, post-meal): 7b 01 20 01 10 dd aa 00 09 1a 0a 11 0d 2d 01 2a 20 11 0e 09 03 0f 7d = 2026-10-17 13:45, raw 1 x 100 + 42 = 142 mg/dL, post-meal, glucose.
Worked (GKI pair, glucose half): 7b 01 20 01 10 dd aa 00 09 1a 0a 11 07 1f 01 08 00 12 02 09 09 0a 7d = 2026-10-17 07:31, 108 mg/dL, general, glucose GKI pair.

Worked (GKI pair, ketone half): 7b 01 20 01 10 dd aa 00 09 1a 0a 11 07 20 01 19 00 56 06 0d 0a 09 7d = 2026-10-17 07:32, raw 125 -> 1.25 mmol/L, ketone GKI pair; with the record before it, GKI = (108 / 18) / 1.25 = 4.8.
Worked (control solution): 7b 01 20 01 10 dd aa 00 09 1a 0a 12 09 05 01 0c 00 22 00 03 0a 03 7d = 2026-10-18 09:05, 112 mg/dL, glucose CONTROL — not a reading.

SerialReply.description: Answer to get_serial, notified on 0003cdd1. 30 bytes; 16 data bytes.

fields.description: Bytes 9-24: 16 ASCII bytes; strip trailing NUL and space padding.
fields.name: serial

fields.description: Bytes 25-28: CRC-16/MODBUS of bytes 1-24 as four nibble bytes. Byte 29 is 7d.
fields.name: check

parse_rules: Find the header 7b 01 20 01 10 77 aa 00 10, take the 16 bytes after it as ASCII and strip NUL and space padding.
Worked: 7b 01 20 01 10 77 aa 00 10 53 4e 30 30 30 54 45 53 54 30 30 30 31 00 00 00 0a 07 01 04 7d = serial SN000TEST0001 (an invented serial; real serials' format is not published).

UnitReply.description: Answer to get_unit, notified on 0003cdd1. 15 bytes; one data byte.

fields.description: Bytes 0-8: 7b 01 20 01 10 aa aa 00 01 (reply, cmd 0xaa, status 0xaa, len 1).
fields.name: header

fields.description: Bytes 10-13: CRC-16/MODBUS of bytes 1-9 as four nibble bytes (low byte first). Byte 14 is 7d.
fields.name: check

parse_rules: Find the 9-byte header 7b 01 20 01 10 aa aa 00 01 and read the next byte. 0x11 means glucose records are mg/dL; 0x22 means they are tenths of mmol/L. Any other code: keep the previously known unit.
The unit applies to glucose and glucose-control records only; ketone is always mmol/L.
Worked (mg/dL): 7b 01 20 01 10 aa aa 00 01 11 0e 0f 07 04 7d = unit 0x11, mg/dL; check 0x74ef.
Worked (mmol/L): 7b 01 20 01 10 aa aa 00 01 22 0a 0f 06 01 7d = unit 0x22, mmol/L; check 0x61af.

check.algorithm: CRC-16/MODBUS (reflected polynomial 0xa001, init 0xffff, no final xor)
check.encoding: Four bytes, low CRC byte first, each CRC byte split into its high nibble then its low nibble, one nibble per byte (values 0x00-0x0f). CRC 0xd821 is sent as 02 01 0d 08.
check.provenance: Derived by this project, not stated by any source: a search over CRC-16 polynomials, inits and nibble orders found exactly this rule reproducing all four literal frames in the integration (three requests and the end-of-records reply). The schema's `auto: crc16_modbus` writes two raw bytes, so it cannot express the nibble split; the known requests carry no data and are declared as fixed frames instead.
check.span: Bytes 1 through the last data byte: everything after 7b and before the check.

frame.constant_bytes: Bytes 1 and 3 are 0x01 in every known frame, both directions; meaning unknown.
frame.layout: 7b | 01 | src | 01 | dst | cmd | status | len_hi | len_lo | data[len] | c0 c1 c2 c3 | 7d
frame.length: uint16, big-endian, counts data bytes only (unit reply 00 01, serial reply 00 10).

hardware.bluetooth: Bluetooth 4.2 LE per the vendor's Canadian product page
hardware.memory_order: Oldest overwritten first when full; the manual shows results newest-first on screen. The order of the BLE dump is not stated.
hardware.power: 2 x AAA LR03; automatic shut-off 2 minutes after the last action

session.notes: The integration's values, a known-good envelope rather than protocol constants. It also waits 180 s after a sync before reacting to the meter's advertisements again, which is client policy.

remaining_unknowns: No entities are bound. Every reply arrives on one notification characteristic, and a 'last glucose' or 'last ketone' sensor would need to pick one record type out of a 1000-record dump, decode a base-100 value (byte14 x 100 + byte15, not a uint16) and choose the newest timestamp. The schema's format/format_match can express none of those three steps, so a client must implement payload_formats.RecordFrame and keep its own history.
Header bytes 5-6 and the length field of a record frame. The client reads only bytes 9-17; the worked examples show dd aa / 00 09 by analogy with the unit and serial replies.
The order in which fetch_all_records returns results (oldest or newest first). The client keeps the meter's order only to find GKI pairs and sorts by timestamp for display.
mmol/L scaling of glucose (raw / 10) is from the client's code but was not tested on hardware: its author's meter is set to mg/dL.
The command the vendor app uses to set the meter's clock during sync, and any command to clear memory. Neither is known; no write beyond the three reads has been seen.
Whether the meter advertises 0003cdd0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b0131 (the client matches by name only).
Whether the vendor app forms an OS-level bond. The open client never bonds and works.
The CRC rule is a derivation from four frames, not a stated fact; a client that cannot verify checks can still parse by position, as the open client does.

characteristics.name: Reply (notify)
characteristics.notes: Every reply arrives here as notifications; enable them before the first write. FRAME: 7b | 01 | src | 01 | dst | cmd | status | len (uint16 big-endian) | data[len] | check (4 bytes) | 7d. Replies carry src 0x20, dst 0x10 (requests the reverse). status is 0xaa on the unit and serial replies, 0x66 on the end-of-records frame. A record frame is 23 bytes, longer than a default 20-byte notification, so a frame may arrive split across notifications: concatenate the notification bytes in order and cut frames at 7b ... 7d (the check is nibble-encoded and record data bytes stay below 0x7b, so neither delimiter occurs inside a frame). Check: CRC-16/MODBUS over bytes 1 through the last data byte, low byte first, each byte sent as two bytes holding its high then low nibble — see protocol_details.frame. The layouts of the unit reply, serial reply and stored-record frame are in payload_formats.

fetch_all_records.description: Ask for every stored result (cmd 0xdd). The meter answers with one RecordFrame per result and then the EndOfRecords frame; the integration allows 30 s. There is no known "since" or "latest only" variant, so a client de-duplicates on (timestamp, type, value) itself.

get_serial.description: Ask for the meter's serial number (cmd 0x77). Answer: payload_formats.SerialReply.

get_unit.description: Ask for the meter's glucose display unit (cmd 0xaa). Answer: payload_formats.UnitReply. Ask before fetching records — a glucose record's scale depends on it.

characteristics.name: Command (write)
characteristics.notes: The integration writes without response; whether the characteristic also accepts write-with-response is not shown. All three known requests have no data (len 00 00), so they are fixed frames; their check bytes are already included.

services.name: VivaChek meter service
services.notes: Vendor service. Its UUID is NOT on the Bluetooth SIG base: the last group is 00805f9b0131, not 00805f9b34fb, so 0003cdd0, 0003cdd1 and 0003cdd2 are full 128-bit vendor UUIDs and must not be shortened to 16-bit forms. The service UUID comes from the integration's README; its code addresses the two characteristics directly.
